idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). I rolled production back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: v2.3.0 in all regions, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 remains unhealthy in production and should not be redeployed until it is fixed. v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging and was not used for the rollback. Next steps: investigate the v2.3.1 failure and confirm checkout traffic is stable on v2.3.0.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent production release that was healthy. v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production. v2.3.1-rc was only in staging, so I didn't use it. Because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production, the change-manager approval policy didn't apply.
- **Result:** checkout-api now reports v2.3.0 in every region, healthy, with an error rate of 0.002, down from 0.18 on v2.3.1.
- **Incident:** The first attempt to open INC-0001 timed out. I checked that no incident had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key, so only one incident exists. It describes the rollback, the post-rollback health, and the next steps.

v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the failure is fixed. Someone still needs to investigate why it failed health checks.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production, and v2.3.1-rc was only in staging. v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, so the approval policy doesn't apply. Rolling back.
